maria gomez: Quick sync — I ran two nsys captures comparing master (before scheduler lifecycle patch) -> HEAD (after). Seeing ~18% extra time attributed to the "wrapper_invoke" region and more small memcpy spikes during KV warmup. Attaching short notes and traces: t1=nsys_master.qdrep, t2=nsys_head.qdrep :point_down:

perf-bot: auto-summary: t2 shows wrapper_invoke up 18% (p50 token latency +12%), small memcpy (cpu->gpu) spikes increased, GPU occupancy similar. See /tmp/nsys-summary-1812345678.txt

chris li: Can you paste the exact commands you used to collect the traces? also which workload (batch dist / seq len)?

maria gomez: sure — workload: mix of short chat (avg seq=64, batch=4) + a minority long-case (seq=1024). commands:
```bash
# trace master
nsys profile -o t1 --capture-range=nvtx --target-processes all --trace=cuda,cudnn,cublas python run_perf.py --model trt-vllm --clients 8 --duration 60
# trace head
nsys profile -o t2 --capture-range=nvtx --target-processes all --trace=cuda,cudnn,cublas python run_perf.py --model trt-vllm --clients 8 --duration 60
```

alex wong: quick greps from the two timelines (timestamps normalized):
- master: wrapper_invoke total 1.7s, scheduler_step 0.5s, trt_infer_kernel 7.8s, kv_copy_host2dev 0.3s
- head:   wrapper_invoke total 2.0s, scheduler_step 0.55s, trt_infer_kernel 7.7s, kv_copy_host2dev 0.9s
Looks like trt kernel time slightly down but memcpy (kv copy) jumped ~3x and wrapper_invoke up ~18%.

chris li: That kv_copy spike is suspicious. Is KV warming done inline in the wrapper now? We added a cache-fill fallback in the scheduler last week. Could be copying extra prefixes synchronously.

maria gomez: I inspected NVTX regions — wrapper_invoke wraps: preproc -> kv_copy -> scheduler_call -> engine_invoke -> postproc. The extra time is inside the kv_copy NVTX bracket.

perf-bot: kernel hotspots (t2):
- memcpy H2D small chunks: 41% of memcpy time (many 4-32KB ops)
- cudaLaunchKernel stalls: minimal
- CPU spin on wrapper lock: visible (samples show user-space spin inside wrapper_lock())

sam taylor: we added per-request cache-miss synchronous copy to avoid stale sticky pointers. That protected correctness but probably causes many tiny H2D copies. For small-batch chat workloads that kills amortization. Suggest: aggregate KV copies into a single batched H2D per request or make async memcpy + stream fence.

alex wong: quick micro-change experiment: switched to aggregated memcpy (single cudaMemcpyAsync for full prefix) + cudaEvent on stream instead of multiple small copies. Results: wrapper_invoke down from 2.0s -> 1.76s, kv_copy_host2dev down 0.9s -> 0.28s, p50 token latency improved ~9%. I pushed a local branch `opt/kv-batch-copy` with the change.

chris li: nice. Any side-effects? concurrency/ordering?

alex wong: one caveat: we need to make sure the scheduler doesn't assume per-chunk readiness. I added an event and waitInStream before engine_invoke; logic is safe for our current scheduler, but if we later stream different KV shards to different streams we need to revisit. Also the async path requires the wrapper to avoid blocking CPU spin; fixed that by yielding on lock.

maria gomez: ran full nsys again on the branch (t3). numbers: wrapper_invoke 1.78s, kv_copy_host2dev 0.32s, trt_infer_kernel 7.75s. End-to-end p95 latency down ~11% vs head. Good signal.

perf-bot: diff summary t2->t3: wrapper_invoke -11%, kv_copy -65%, cpu spin samples -70%. GPU occupancy unchanged.

sam taylor: next steps:
- cherrypick kv-batch-copy to canary and run longer soak (24h) with mixed traffic
- add unit tests for scheduler assumptions around per-chunk readiness
- consider telemetry to count small H2D memcpy occurrences per request so we can alert if regressions reappear

chris li: agree. Also let's audit the kernel selection fallback we added — it may cause extra fallback codepath that triggers peripheral memops. I can run a targeted trace where we force the autoselect fallback to verify.

maria gomez: OK I'll coordinate canary and schedule the autoselect-fallback trace. Also will add a lightweight stat to the console: "small_kv_copies_per_minute" so SRE can watch.

alex wong: FYI I kept the experiments small — one thing to watch: if a request has many tiny prefix patches (rare), our aggregated copy increases temporary GPU memory footprint. I added a guard to fallback to chunked copies when predicted additional GPU mem > 20% of model KV buffer.

chris li: sounds safe. If the guard trips often we can revisit layout or compress small patches.

maria gomez: thanks all. I'll open a PR for `opt/kv-batch-copy` with the nsys summary attached and link the canary run once scheduled. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: created ticket PERF-7422 linking traces t1,t2,t3 and attachments.
